sketches.title: Garden Court
sketches.premise: You are rival powers in a back garden, and each turn you lay down one living or made thing that takes control of what stands before it. The garden is your arena: roots crack paving, rain drowns fire, and a mower makes short work of weeds. The Judge decides whether your latest thing truly overcomes the last.
sketches.criterion: A move wins by physically defeating, stopping, consuming, trapping, or changing the standing thing; merely hiding, surviving, being a bigger copy, or naming a poetic resemblance loses.
sketches.move_shape: Say what you are and the plain action that beats the last thing: "I am a mole, tunneling under the concrete and breaking its bed."
sketches.first_card: I am a sunflower, turning its gold face toward the sun.

sketches.title: Shed Lockdown
sketches.premise: The garden shed is under siege, and players alternate placing one ordinary garden object into a growing defense or attack plan. Your object must directly defeat the last object by locking it out, cutting it off, breaking it, or making it useless. The Judge treats the chain like a tiny tactical battle, not a poetry contest with muddy boots.
sketches.criterion: The new object must directly prevent, disable, remove, or overpower the previous object in the shed situation; dodging it, merely enduring it, using a larger version, or citing a related cousin does not count.
sketches.move_shape: Name one object and its direct job: "I am a padlock, sealing the toolbox so the thief's screwdriver is useless."
sketches.first_card: I am a key, opening the shed door.

sketches.title: Pest Patrol
sketches.premise: One player introduces a garden nuisance and the other answers with a creature, tool, or garden substance that stops it. Keep escalating through the food chain and household cupboard: slug, bird, cat, fence, salt, rain, and beyond. The Judge accepts a clean counter, then announces the defeat with the dignity of a royal gardener who has just discovered a dead beetle in his salad.
sketches.criterion: Your answer must actively catch, kill, block, wash away, poison, or otherwise stop the pest or threat in front of you; fleeing, hiding, surviving, using a bigger version, or offering a same-family relative is a loss.
sketches.move_shape: Name the counter and its mechanism: "I am a thrush, stabbing the slug and swallowing the smug little slime tube."
sketches.first_card: I am a slug, chewing holes in the lettuce.

sketches.title: Weather War
sketches.premise: The back garden becomes a miniature sky, where each turn summons one weather force or weather-made condition that defeats the last. Sun dries puddles, frost kills seedlings, wind scatters smoke, and rain puts out flames. Grand meteorological nonsense is welcome, but the Judge demands an actual mechanism rather than a thunderous metaphor wearing a fake moustache.
sketches.criterion: The new weather state must directly cancel, transform, scatter, freeze, melt, drown, or otherwise defeat the previous one; avoiding it, merely lasting longer, making it bigger, or calling it its stormy cousin fails.
sketches.move_shape: State the weather and its action: "I am frost, freezing the puddle solid and strangling the tender roots beneath it."
sketches.first_card: I am rain, drumming across the garden beds.

sketches.title: Toolbox Trial
sketches.premise: Every turn, choose one familiar garden tool or material that defeats the tool or material before it. A shovel buries a hose, a saw cuts a stick, and glue ruins a clean break. The Judge is the stern foreman of this ridiculous hardware duel, and will not let a fancy speech turn a rake into a dragon.
sketches.criterion: The new item must use its ordinary function to cut, crush, bind, block, bury, damage, or disable the previous item; dodging, outlasting, choosing a bigger copy, or naming a related tool without a mechanism loses.
sketches.move_shape: Name the item and its ordinary action: "I am wire, binding the garden shears shut before they can bite."
sketches.first_card: I am a garden hose, spraying a cold arc over the paving.

sketches.title: Night Garden
sketches.premise: The garden changes as evening falls: each turn names one thing that reveals, frightens, traps, feeds on, or destroys what stands before it. A torch exposes a hiding fox, a cat catches a mouse, and dawn ends the night. The Judge gives every victory a theatrical verdict, as though the compost heap were a haunted castle and your move had just insulted its ancestors.
sketches.criterion: Your thing must directly reveal, scare away, catch, consume, block, or transform the standing thing; merely hiding, surviving, being a larger version, or using a figurative phrase without a real mechanism is defeat.
sketches.move_shape: Name the thing and its action: "I am a torch, shining through the hedge and exposing the burglar's muddy face."
sketches.first_card: I am a mouse, creeping beneath the dark flowerpots.
